questions.q: What type of fear does Michelle Obama describe as rational and protective?
questions.why: She defines protective fear as rational and keeping you safe.

questions.q: Which tool did Obama's father eventually use to stay mobile?
questions.why: He progressed from cane to crutches to a motorized cart.

questions.q: What three-step method does Obama recommend for acute fear?
questions.why: She outlines breathing, reflecting, then planning.

questions.q: How did Obama feel when Barack announced his presidential run?
a: Apprehensive about losing their Chicago life
Excited to start a new adventure
Confident it would improve their family
questions.why: She was uneasy about upending their stable life.

questions.q: What common misconception about fear does Obama highlight?
a: It often works quietly, not as panic
It is always loud and obvious
It only appears in big decisions
questions.why: She notes fear usually sabotages us subtly.
